Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:
- Policy stance: The intermeeting 50 bp cut, lower IOER, ongoing T‑bill purchases, and term/overnight repo operations aim to keep funding markets liquid and reserves ample, supporting transmission and policy implementation.
- SLOOS signal on credit supply: Banks reported tighter standards and other terms on C&I loans and construction/land development loans, reduced credit limits, and higher credit score thresholds. They also indicated reduced risk tolerance and expected further tightening in 2020 across C&I (including medium-market firms) and CRE segments.
- SLOOS signal on credit demand/performance: Weaker demand was reported in construction and land development; demand for some consumer credit (e.g., credit cards) was unchanged, offering only a modest offset. Banks expected deterioration in loan portfolios, collateral values, and HELOCs.
- Implication: Even with supportive Fed actions to stabilize funding markets, SLOOS points to tightening credit availability and worsening expected loan performance, which could amplify the negative shock from COVID‑19 through business investment and household credit channels.

Net tone: supportive policy actions but a darker near‑term outlook given tightening bank standards and expected deterioration flagged by SLOOS.
